problem_context: Current generative modeling approaches face fundamental challenges in mapping from one distribution to another efficiently. While discriminative models simply map individual samples to labels, generative models must learn mappings between entire distributions - a significantly more complex task. Existing methods often require iterative procedures at inference time, performing multiple network evaluations to progressively transform samples from noise to data. This creates a trade-off between generation quality and computational efficiency. There is a need for generative models that can produce high-quality samples in a single forward pass, without sacrificing the modeling capacity that makes iterative methods successful. The challenge is to find a training paradigm that can learn complex distribution mappings without requiring iterative refinement during generation. A key insight is that neural network training inherently updates parameters iteratively - what if we could view this training process as evolving the output distribution itself, rather than just optimizing a fixed objective? Consider how the distribution of generated samples changes as training progresses.
desirable_properties: Should generate high-quality samples in a single forward pass
Should be trainable from scratch without requiring pre-trained models
Should scale effectively to high-resolution data
Should avoid mode collapse and capture the full data distribution
Should support conditional generation with flexible conditioning
Should work across different data modalities beyond just images
Should have a principled mechanism that governs how generated samples move or change position during training iterations
Should define an equilibrium condition where generated samples stop moving when the output distribution matches the data distribution
Should use direct interactions between individual generated samples and individual real data samples to determine how samples should move
Should ensure that the movement mechanism has mathematical properties that guarantee equilibrium is reached only when distributions match
field_context: Generative modeling is a fundamental problem in machine learning that aims to learn the underlying distribution of data and generate new samples from it. This field has seen rapid progress with various paradigms including adversarial training, variational approaches, and iterative refinement methods, each with their own trade-offs between sample quality, training stability, and inference efficiency. Recent work has explored various ways to reduce inference-time computation, but most still rely on some form of iterative refinement or adversarial dynamics. An underexplored direction is how the training process itself evolves distributions over time.
